cases.reason: The system correctly recognized a progress update that explicitly required no reply and produced no suggestion card. For Alex, this supports attention management by avoiding an unnecessary interruption.

The Later classification respects the nonblocking request, but automatically generating a draft for a task that can wait may add review burden. The request is relevant to Alex's responsibilities, yet its low urgency makes the benefit less clear.

The system correctly treated the rehearsal request as urgent, detected the conflict with Alex's availability, and proposed a reply that did not accept 10:20. It also connected the request to the room-booking dependency and cited the source utterance.

Showing the original utterance, rationale, uncertainties, and editable draft gives Alex useful context for judging whether the recommendation is appropriate. This makes the generated response inspectable rather than opaque.

Alex could replace the draft with wording that preserves the 10:30 arrival constraint, offers 10:40 rehearsal participation, and asks the team to confirm before booking. Confirmation and copying succeeded while the interface clearly indicated that Alex still had to send or mark the message sent.

Requiring renewed confirmation after editing protects against accidentally treating an unreviewed revision as sent. However, the clipboard still contains the earlier confirmed version, creating a meaningful risk that Alex could send text different from the currently visible draft.

The new alert appropriately notices that room booking is outside Alex's responsibilities and that the speaker is unidentified. Its uncertainty is explicit, but the summary says the 10:20 issue was 'already handled via Alex's confirmed reply,' which may overstate completion because the reply was only copied and was not sent. The suggested response also combines a timing issue with a separate booking-approval issue that may not be directed at Alex.

Stopping the session disabled further input and analysis, froze elapsed time, and preserved records. This gives Alex a clear stopping point and reduces the chance of unintended processing after the session ends.

selective_attention.reason: Within this trace, the system distinguished no-reply information, deferrable work, and an urgent request linked to a booking dependency.

context_for_correct_reply.reason: The system used Alex's profile constraints, the source text, role boundaries, and explicit uncertainties to support a reply that avoided accepting the impossible time.

control_over_commitments.reason: Editing, confirmation, and the visible requirement to send preserve user control, but the stale clipboard and summary wording could cause confusion about which version is current and whether anything was actually sent.

best_fit: Text-based meeting streams where requests may interrupt work, depend on personal availability, or risk accidental commitments.
poor_fit: Low-stakes conversations where generated drafts create more review work than value, and situations requiring reliable audio attribution or actual message delivery, which this trace did not test.

biggest_benefit.text: Meeting Cue can filter attention and turn a time-conflicting request into a cautious, editable response without making Alex accept an impossible commitment.

biggest_risk.text: The workflow can leave Alex uncertain about whether the latest edited wording, the earlier clipboard content, or the exported status represents the actionable message.

improvements.suggestion: Make every status and summary explicitly distinguish draft, confirmed, copied, sent, and marked sent; never describe a copied response as handled or completed.
Invalidate or replace the clipboard when the draft is edited, and show a prominent warning that the clipboard contains an older version until the current wording is reconfirmed and copied.
Reduce draft generation for deferrable requests and offer a clearer clarification action when a request comes from an unidentified speaker or may not be directed at Alex.

safe_final_reply: I cannot make 10:20 AM tomorrow. I can arrive at 10:30 and join the rehearsal at 10:40. Please check whether 10:40 works for everyone before booking. This is a draft for your confirmation; it has not been sent.
presentation_claim: In this recorded text-only workflow, Meeting Cue demonstrated selective attention, profile-aware conflict detection, editable response drafting, and confirmation before copying.
not_established: The trace does not establish human productivity gains, user satisfaction, audio-recognition accuracy, reliable speaker identification in live meetings, message delivery, timing performance, or usefulness across other meeting types. No comparison group or independently verified human task outcome is available.
